transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-18
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Sunridge Head of Platform), James Lee (SRE), Olivia Park (CTO)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Redwood rate limiting and multi-tenant controls (org & project keys) with emphasis on quotas, per-route limits, and enterprise controls (SSO, RBAC, KMS). Demo of Console + API flows and discussion of POC/benchmarks.

Topics:
- Org vs Project keys and mapping to tenants
- Rate limits, quotas, and burst handling
- Per-route/token cost controls and monitoring
- Security: SAML/SSO, SOC2, KMS, audit logs
- POC next steps and benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have the usual suspects, I will hand off to Priya for the demo but quick intro - Redwood is focused on inference serving, low latency and predictable costs, today we'll go through rate limits, org/project keys and how you can control usage across teams.
[00:22] Maya Thompson (Sunridge): Thanks Alex, high level we want to understand how we can allocate budget/quotas to different product teams, and ensure a noisy team doesn't blow past monthly commits. Also compliance and SSO are big.
[00:35] Priya Rao (Redwood): Great, that's exactly what org and project keys solve. I'll share my screen - starting in the Console, under Org settings you can see overall org quotas, then under Projects you create project-level API keys. Each key gets its own quota and rate limit policy.
[01:10] James Lee (Sunridge): Quick question - how are rate limits enforced? Is it per-API-key at the edge or per-model backend? We have auto-scaling pools and worried about throttling causing retries.
[01:28] Priya Rao: Good question. We enforce a combination: edge middleware checks token counts and per-key QPS, and the router also applies backpressure to the serving runtime. So you get immediate 429s at the edge when a key hits its limit. For certain Dedicated setups you can opt for soft-limits with queuing and graceful degradation.
[02:05] Olivia Park (Sunridge): When you say token counts, is that per-request tokens or aggregated? We bill and quota by tokens so need alignment.
[02:17] Alex Chen: It's per-token. Policies can be expressed as monthly token quotas, daily quotas, or QPS limits. We also expose per-route constraints, so you can say different endpoints (e.g., embedding vs generation) have separate budgets.
[03:02] Priya Rao: Showing the policy editor now - you can create a policy that caps project key X to 10M tokens/month, with a burst allowance of 500 RPS for 2 minutes. There's a preview mode that simulates consumption. Note: UI labels sometimes say "org key" in older builds, you might see a mismatch if you're on cached assets.
[04:00] Maya Thompson: Can keys be rotated automatically and scoped to specific models or regions? We want keys that only allow access to a smaller set of models for regulatory reasons.
[04:12] Priya Rao: Yes. Keys are scopeable - model allowlist, and region constraints are supported for Hosted and Dedicated. For Private (VPC) deploys we support local enforcement. Rotation can be automated via the API and we emit audit events for key creation/rotation.
[05:00] James Lee: How does multi-tenant isolation work? If an org has multiple projects, can one project affect another via KV cache or shared GPU pools?
[05:18] Priya Rao: By default projects are logically isolated - KV cache entries are tagged per-project, and serving runtime isolates KV caches per session. For Dedicated you get physical pool isolation if requested. There are tradeoffs: shared pools improve utilization and lower cost, but require stricter quotas and fallback rules.
[06:05] Alex Chen: We often recommend start with shared pool + strict quotas, then move high-risk teams to dedicated pools.
[06:20] Maya: That sounds good. Can you demo the API usage for creating a project key and applying a quota?
[06:35] Priya Rao: Sure - curl example: POST /orgs/{org_id}/projects -> create project; then POST /keys with scope project_id and policy JSON. Example policy has fields: allowed_models, monthly_tokens, per_minute_qps. Forgive me if the sample JSON on screen is a bit messy, the export sometimes strips commas.
[08:00] [Priya walks through a live curl demo and shows request/response - small stutter in transcript]
[09:20] Priya Rao: When a key exceeds quota the API returns 429 with a body explaining remaining reset time, and the Console will flag the key as throttled. We also support webhook notifications if you want pro-active alerts.
[10:15] James Lee: If we need soft-throttles to avoid client errors, can you do token-bucket style throttling that returns degraded results instead of 429?
[10:30] Priya Rao: There are two mechanisms: soft-limit where requests are queued for a short period (configurable) and automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant. For example, if gpt-like model is rate limited, we can route to a quantized variant with lower token cost. That's part of our smart routing.
[11:05] Olivia Park: On the security side, we need SOC 2 and SAML integrations to map our Okta groups to project permissions. Is that part of the product?
[11:18] Alex Chen: Yes - SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning available, RBAC with project roles (admin, dev, billing only), and audit logs that record API key use and policy changes. We'll share the SOC 2 report and SAML setup docs after this call.
[12:00] Maya: Also KMS - we use AWS KMS for key wrapping. How does Redwood handle customer-managed keys?
[12:10] Priya Rao: We support customer KMS for Dedicated and Private installs. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in some enterprise plans. We'll follow up with the security whitepaper that details the architecture.
[13:00] [00:13:45 in call - minor background noise; James stepping away briefly]
[15:05] Priya Rao: Back to quotas - Console shows historical usage and projections. You can set alarms at percentage thresholds and auto-execute policies like reduce per-route QPS or disable expensive models when threshold hit.
[16:00] Maya: Can thresholds be team-specific and notify Slack channel per project?
[16:12] Priya Rao: Yes, alerting hooks include email, Slack, PagerDuty, and webhooks. You can configure per-project alert recipients.
[18:00] Alex Chen: On the billing side, we can report token-level cost by project or route. That helps cost allocation to internal teams. You mentioned you want budget controls - we can generate monthly cap enforcement and soft-allowance windows for events.
[19:10] James Lee: For the POC, we'd like a baseline test: 1) run 30-minute synthetic load with both generation and embeddings, 2) measure per-token latency and cost under shared pool, 3) validate quotas and fallback to quantized models. Would Redwood run that or provide scripts?
[19:35] Priya Rao: We provide a benchmark script and can help run the first baseline with our SE support. I'll attach the script to the follow-up.
[20:00] Maya: Any limitations around project key count? We have hundreds of microservices and may want a key per service.
[20:12] Priya Rao: You can create thousands of keys programmatically, but for manageability we often recommend grouping services into logical projects then use ephemeral tokens for per-service auth.
[21:05] Olivia Park: How does everything look on Dedicated vs Hosted for rate-limits? We prefer Dedicated for predictable latency.
[21:20] Alex Chen: Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and stricter tail-latency SLOs. Rate limiting still applies but with higher thresholds and you can configure autoscale policies. Hosted is easier to get started and has flexible scaling but slightly more variable tail latency.
[22:00] James Lee: Any gotchas on KV cache leakage across tenants? We've seen shared caches leak prefixes before with other vendors.
[22:15] Priya Rao: We partition KV cache by project id; for older model adapters there were edge cases, but current runtime tags entries and clears them on project deletion. We can show you the eviction metrics in the POC.
[23:00] [small interjection from Maya: "can we see logs?" starts at 23:05]
[23:05] Priya Rao: Yes, audit logs include key usage, API responses and policy evals. Retention configurable per contract.
[24:00] Alex Chen: Let's talk about SLOs and SLA: for Dedicated we offer an SLA that covers uptime and latency percentiles. For Hosted we publish performance profiles per model.
[25:40] Maya: Will you share sample performance reports?
[25:50] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll attach the performance deck and a sample report. Note there can be small naming mismatches in older docs where "Redwood Optimize" is referenced as "Redwood Ops" - ignore that, it's the same feature.
[27:30] Priya Rao: Demoing the API again - showing how to update a policy via PATCH, and how Console reflects changes in near real-time. A note: if you update a quota policy while requests are in flight, enforcement applies immediately for new requests.
[29:00] James Lee: Can we do scheduled policy changes (e.g., Monday 00:00 adjust quotas for a promotion)?
[29:12] Priya Rao: Scheduled policy changes are supported via the API; you can set effective_from timestamps on policy objects.
[31:00] Maya: For regulatory reasons we may need regional isolation - are there region-specific keys or project scoping?
[31:15] Priya Rao: Project scoping supports region constraints. Also for Private deployments you can host the runtime entirely within your VPC. We'll include network diagrams in the follow-up pack.
[33:00] [brief pause; Alex paraphrases next steps]
[33:10] Alex Chen: Recap: 1) We'll send pricing and examples for org/project key policies; 2) Priya will send the POC runbook and benchmark scripts; 3) Sunridge will share usage dashboard + SSO details; 4) schedule pilot kickoff.
[34:05] Maya: Sounds good. A couple of other smaller asks: SOC 2 report, SAML setup guide, and sample audit log export format.
[34:20] Alex Chen: We'll attach those - SOC 2 and our security whitepaper plus a CSV sample of audit logs.
[35:00] James Lee: One last technical nit - when fallback to quantized variant happens, are there semantic differences in outputs we should expect?
[35:12] Priya Rao: There can be slight variations; we provide evaluation diffs and quality thresholds. In Optimize we can pin certain critical prompts to always use the high-quality model and route less critical traffic to quantized variants.
[36:00] Olivia Park: Great. Cost controls are a big win for us. How long until POC can start if we get materials today?
[36:10] Alex Chen: We can start baseline within a week of finalizing scope - so looking at week of 2026-09-28 if we get the usage exports and SSO details this week.
[37:00] Maya: We'll aim to get you the dashboard by end of Friday.
[37:10] Priya Rao: Perfect. I'll also include example policies and a sample script to create project keys at scale.
[39:00] [small cross-talk about calendar availability]
[41:00] Alex Chen: Any blockers or questions we didn't cover?
[41:10] James Lee: None immediate, just want to validate the benchmark results.
[41:25] Maya Thompson: No blockers. Thanks for the detail, this was helpful.
[42:00] Alex Chen: Great - next steps in the notes. We'll send follow-ups and book the pilot kickoff. Thanks everyone.
[44:30] Call end.
